title: Coal stocks at thermal plants hold above 18 MT as supply deficit narrows
summary: The daily requirement of coal for domestic thermal power plants is less than 3 MT per day. They account for more than 60% of the power generated during peak hours.

title: Anti-CEC row LIVE: Delhi Police denotify Jantar Mantar as protest site; suggest three new locations
summary: INDIA bloc starts its march from Barakhamba intersection at Connaught Place; sources say CJI Surya Kant declined a request by Rahul Gandhi for a meeting as the issues were already sub judice

title: Caste discrimination during SC man’s burial: Protest in Erode seeks action against officials
summary: The protesters demanded that officials be held accountable under the SC/ST Prevention of Atrocities Act for their alleged failure to prevent the humiliation meted out to members of an SC community

title: ‘Unacceptable’: CJP on Jantar Mantar being denotified as protest site
summary: Attacking the Prime Minister, Saurav Das said that said soon the government would denotify India as a democracy.

title: Tested by mud and water, in Bundelkhand
summary: After months of protests in Chhatarpur district over the Ken-Betwa river link project, the next leg of the jal satyagraha by tribal people in Madhya Pradesh’s Bundelkhand will soon complete a month. Hundreds affected by the State government’s Majhgaon irrigation project are protesting in Panna district, seeking fair compensation and rehabilitation while alleging irregularities in the process. Mehul Malpani gauges the anger and frustration of those who say their movement is being crushed by force

title: Female elephant trapped in slush at Erode district’s Gunderi­pallam reservoir dies
summary: The elephant had come to the reservoir to drink water when it became trapped in the slush and was unable to move

title: Prem Anand Sinha takes charge as DVAC chief
summary: He served as Commissioner of Police, Tambaram, before taking charge as DVAC Director

title: Corruption case: Supreme Court directs no coercive action be taken against people linked to Punjab govt
summary: The Supreme Court declined to stay the FIR but barred coercive steps, as the Punjab government challenges a High Court order directing a CBI probe into corruption allegations
